facts: The Order of the Court was as follows: Ten appellants have been convicted by the trial court for the offences u/s. 302 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code besides Ss. 147 and 148 IPC and S. 27 of the Arms Act.
All of them were grievance of the appellants is that they should be heard before they are dispossessed.
The prosecution case, in short, is the following: deceased Nathun Gope was a peon attached to a High School.
On 11-4-1987, when the deceased was proceeding to the school during morning hours all the ten accused waylaid him.
Internally there was blood in left pleural cavity with laceration on the left lower lobe of lung and fracture of fifth to seventh ribs.
petitioner_arguments: If the intention was to murder the deceased at least A-1 would have fired the gun.
11 out of 12 injuries did not cause any damage to the internal organs.
The common intention of the assailants was only to thrash the deceased and to inflict him with injuries.
court_reasoning: There is no scope for disturbing the finding of the two courts that all the ten persons were involved in the attack made on the deceased at the time and place alleged by the prosecution.

The aforesaid arguments based on the abovementioned two broad features is a strong circumstance for us to think that the common intention of the assailants was only to thrash the deceased and to inflict him with injuries.
We, therefore, alter the conviction from S. 302 IPC to S. 304 Part II IPC.
holding: The appeal is disposed of accordingly.
Hence we therefore, convict the appellant for the said offence read with S. 149 IPC instead of S. 302 IPC.
The sentence passed on the other counts will remain undisturbed and they will run concurrently.
